problems: The shorter Messenger has conspicuous horizontal striping across the hood opening, consistent with retained hair intersecting the hood.
The Market Elder’s upright cylindrical crown and narrow brim read as a top hat, suggesting the Industrial Age rather than an unmistakably medieval cap.
The King’s lower robe reads as two straight trouser legs. The Breadmaker and Elder also need stronger gown silhouettes without rigid geometry bridging their moving legs.

In this view, the caravan leader reads clearly as a jester but less clearly as a visitor from another court. The small heraldic details and rear travel bundle do little to establish that distinction at stream scale.

ALL LONG GARMENTS READ AS TROUSERS (Breadmaker gown, Market Elder robe, King robe). Each 'skirt' is built as two separate legL/legR boxes, so a vertical gap and seam runs down the middle. On the Breadmaker the apron is also split into two leg panels, so she reads as a red top over cream pyjama trousers rather than a long wool dress with an apron. The Elder reads as red or green trousers and the King as blue trousers. This is today's clothes recoloured, the biggest age-read failure on the sheet.

Market Elder hat: the hat:dark cylinder (brim 0.42, crown 0.28 wide x 0.20 tall, straight sides) renders as a modern/Victorian top hat, mustard on one wearer and brown on the other. The bible's avoid list rules out Victorian, so this is anachronistic.
Carpenter mallet: the head is a 0.29 x 0.145 x 0.16 slab in pale linen #c5c0a8 on a short handle. It reads as a white book, tablet or brick held out at the side, not a wooden mallet.

Carpenter fallen cowl: the hips box at y 0.6 in hat:dark becomes a mustard neck-pillow ring around the face on the red wearer and nearly vanishes on the green one. Its back parts (on the cape bone) are invisible from the front. The kit has no headgear, so the base hair block sits on the head like a dark fez or stovepipe. From above, the Carpenter is just a box with a brown front.
Carpenter: the brown apron (#8b6240), brown hose (#8b6240) and dark-brown shoes merge into one brown lower half, so the apron edge is lost.
Carpenter and Young Messenger have the same overall shape: knee tunic in shirt colour, dark legs and something brown at the hip. In a crowd from above, only the hood separates them.

Fixed #416c48 green on the Elder's mantle and the Messenger's hood vanishes on a green-shirted wearer. On the second figures, mantle/tunic and hood/tunic merge into one green blob, and the dagged collar is lost.

Young Messenger: the hood point and liripipe cannot be seen. The cone sits at the back of the head and the liripipe is a 0.075-wide strip on the cape bone. From the front the hood reads as a boxy green helmet with a small stub on top. The sealed scroll (0.085 x 0.29 cylinder) is a tiny white peg lost against the satchel.

King: the 'sceptre' is a 0.42 rod angled forward with a gold sphere at hip height. On screen the rod is invisible and he looks like he is holding a gold ball or orange beside his belt, so the symbol of office is weak. The crown, ermine collar and clasp are good.

King and Jester share the same dominant colours: blue #405e8b with ivory #e5d8b6. Side by side, and certainly as small figures from 40 degrees above, both read as 'blue-and-white figure'. The leader needs to look foreign, not like the King's household.

Jester fit: the red court-badge diamond on the hips bone at [-0.2, 0.625] sits on top of the shoulder beside the head and reads as a red ear or fin. The sleeve patch on armL at z 0.11 floats about 3 cm off the 0.15-deep sleeve and shows as a loose brown square. The marotte head is a skin-coloured sphere with tiny cones and reads as a held flesh ball. The curled toes are barely visible.
fix:
Carpenter: Keep the short split tunic, waist apron, fallen cowl and broad mallet head; these distinguish the trade well. Give the cowl a consistent contrasting wool colour so it remains readable on both wearer palettes, and keep the mallet handle visibly seated in the hand. Breadmaker: Keep the coif, waist-only cream apron and chunky loaf. Add modest outward flare to each leg-bound gown panel, preserve clearance between the inner edges, and expose a clear shoe strip beneath the hem. Market Elder: Replace the stacked brim-and-cylinder hat with a low, broad, asymmetric soft cap or folded medieval bonnet. Retain the forked staff and mantle clasp; add leg-bound outer hem flare and ensure the green mantle contrasts with green shirts. Young Messenger: Add hair to hide, then fit the hood shell cleanly around both heads. Check the head-bound hood and cape-bound liripipe remain connected through head turns; preserve the strong dagged shoulder edge, satchel and tall boots. King: Keep the crown, blue-and-red palette and pale mantle collar. Broaden the robe toward its outer lower edges using separate leg-bound panels, add a substantial gold hem band, and avoid a rigid skirt spanning both legs. Make the sceptre shaft more visible beyond the fist so it reads as an office-bearing object rather than an isolated gold ball. Caravan leader: Preserve the excellent three-point cap and large ivory-blue divisions. Enlarge the split-diamond foreign-court badge onto a broad shoulder tab and repeat it on the travel pack; make the rolled bundle visible beside the upper torso from the gameplay camera. Keep this heraldry exclusive to the travelling court. / GENERAL: never build a skirt, gown or robe from legL/legR boxes. Make the long body garment one piece on the hips bone, a little flared, with "trousers" hidden. For example, upper skirt hips box [0,-0.20,0] size [0.52,0.40,0.36]; lower skirt hips box [0,-0.52,0] size [0.58,0.40,0.42] (hem at about -0.72, about 8 cm above the ground); then a 0.05-tall hem band in a contrasting colour at y -0.70. Shoes may stay visible below. Any apron is ONE hips panel at z +0.215 (just in front of the 0.42-deep skirt), never two leg strips. For hoods, mantles and capes, use a role that contrasts with "shirt" ("accent", "pants" or "shirt:dark") or a fixed palette colour, so they never merge with the tunic.

CARPENTER: remove the cowl ring at the neck. Give him a wide straw work hat: head cylinder brim at [0,0.33,0] size [0.50,0.04,0.48] in #d6af55, plus a low crown cylinder at [0,0.40,0] size [0.30,0.12,0.28] in #c5c0a8. This is a strong round silhouette from above, unlike every other kit. Rebuild the mallet in wood: armR handle cylinder at [0,-0.55,0.06] size [0.05,0.32,0.05] in #5c4030, head cylinder (rotation z 1.5708) at [0,-0.72,0.06] size [0.13,0.24,0.13] in #8b6240, so it reads as a barrel mallet hanging from the hand. Alternatively carry it over the shoulder on armR at rotation x -2.6 so it shows above the shoulder line. Make the hose "pants" (or #7b827f grey) and give the apron a 0.03 #5c4030 border so the apron separates from the legs. Optional: a rolled sleeve or tool loop on the belt.

BREADMAKER: hide ["hat","hair","accessory","trousers"]. Replace all six leg-mounted gown and apron parts with the single flared hips skirt from GENERAL, in "shirt". Add one long hips apron panel at [0,-0.36,0.215] size [0.40,0.70,0.03] in #e5d8b6, with the waist tie as it is now. Keep the coif and the loaf; they read well. Optional: a small kerchief/shawl box over the shoulders in "accent" to vary her top from the Elder.

MARKET ELDER: replace the top hat with a soft rounded felt hood or chaperon. For example, a head box [0,0.30,-0.02] size [0.36,0.14,0.34] in "hat", plus a sphere [0,0.36,-0.04] size [0.34,0.16,0.32] for a pudding crown, plus a short cloth tail on the cape bone. Or use the beard-coif as it is with a low round skullcap. NO straight-sided cylinder crowns. The robe goes to the ankle as a single hips skirt in "shirt:dark" (GENERAL). Set the mantle to "accent", or to fixed #8b6240 brown wool, so it never matches the tunic, and widen it to 0.66 so it overhangs the shoulders and gives a broad top-down shape. Keep the forked staff and the beard; they are the kit's best features.

YOUNG MESSENGER: set the hood and dagged collar to "accent", or to fixed #d6af55/#9e443e, so they contrast with the tunic. Give the hood a real point: a cone on the head bone at [0,0.42,-0.12] size [0.20,0.30,0.20] tipped back (rotation x -0.6). Then add the liripipe as a long strip continuing from it down the back: cape bone [0,-0.05,-0.02] size [0.10,0.60,0.06]. Make the dagged collar points larger (0.15) so the zig-zag reads from above. Enlarge the scroll to a cylinder of size [0.10,0.30,0.10] held across the chest (rotation z 1.5708) with a bigger red seal, or swap it for a short message staff. Keep the diagonal strap, satchel and tall boots.

KING: replace the orb-at-hip with a real sceptre. Put a vertical gold rod on armR at [0,-0.30,0.12] size [0.05,0.80,0.05] (top above the shoulder), with a finial sphere at [0,0.12,0.12] size [0.14,0.14,0.14] in #d6af55 and a small cross or three cones on top. Make the robe one ankle-length hips skirt in #405e8b with a gold hem band, not leg boxes. Make the red cloak wider (0.78) and visible from the front by letting its side panels flare out past the arms. Keep the crown, ermine collar with spots, gold clasp and cuffs.

JESTER (LEADER): recolour the motley away from the King's blue and ivory. Use saffron #d6af55 against green #416c48, or saffron against red #9e443e, with ivory kept only for small trim. Recolour the cap horns to match, and enlarge the bells to 0.09. Make the cap horns droop (rotation about ±2.1) so their ends hang with bells beside the cheeks. Move the court-badge diamond from the shoulder top to the chest (hips [-0.12,0.32,0.17]) or the hat front, and delete the parts at hips [-0.2, 0.595-0.641]. Push the armL sleeve patch to z 0.085 and the legR patch flush. Enlarge the curled shoe toes to about [0.13,0.16,0.20] turned up 1.2 rad, with a bell on the tip. Make the marotte a 0.5 stick held up in front of the chest, with a head sphere in #e5d8b6 (not skin) wearing its own two-colour cap of larger cones (0.12).
